memory_lessons.claim: The coalesced control was valid at 0.0234084123 s mean over three samples; the 16x32, K-depth-32 tiled candidate was valid at 0.0228994478 s mean over three samples. The difference is small and remains an observed comparison, not proof that tiling improves performance.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this contrasting 32x16, K-depth-16 candidate with the same correctness checks and repeated-timing protocol, then compare its samples and correctness to both valid candidates.

proposal.hypothesis: The valid 16x32 output tile with K depth 32 measured 0.0228994 s, while the valid coalesced untiled control measured 0.0234084 s. This contrasting 32x16 output tile with K depth 16 keeps one output per thread and contiguous column segments, while halving the shared-memory tile footprint; it also narrows each warp's column span, reverses operand reuse, and doubles K-loop iterations. Correctness and repeated timing will test that tradeoff without assuming a speedup.

retained: Replaced the baseline kernel with a 32-row by 16-column output tile and a K depth of 16, contrasting with the measured 16x32, K-depth-32 tile.
Mapped each thread to one output; threadIdx.x spans the 16 output columns and threadIdx.y spans 32 rows.
Cooperatively staged A and B tiles into shared memory with synchronous barriers, zero-filled K and matrix tails, and used a guarded K-loop increment.

Used size_t for matrix element offsets and quotient/remainder grid calculations; retained the run signature, default-stream launch, alpha/beta semantics, and unused scratch parameter without adding allocations or libraries.

proposal.hypothesis: The catalog has two distinct valid T1 programs: the coalesced one-output-per-thread control averaged 0.0234084 s, while the 16x32-output, K-depth-32 tile averaged 0.0228994 s. That small observed difference does not establish a tiling benefit. This contrasting 8x32-output, K-depth-16 tile keeps a full warp on contiguous output columns while using 256 threads per CTA; it tests whether a smaller row tile and CTA help occupancy, against the costs of less row reuse and more K-loop synchronization. Correctness and repeated timing remain for the controller to evaluate.

retained: Changed the CTA output tile to 8 rows by 32 columns with one output per thread and lanes spanning contiguous columns.
Staged A and B cooperatively in synchronous shared memory with K depth 16; masked input tails and synchronized before and after accumulation.
Retained the existing entry point, default-stream launch, alpha/beta semantics, and unused scratch buffer; added no allocation or external math-library call.
